guide.victory: Assault of Gallus: the Romans win by controlling ten Built-up hexes at the end of any Judaean Melee Phase (control = last occupant [18.3]); the Judaeans win by preventing that through the end of turn 10. The engine tracks hex control and the Built-up count live.

source_defects.note: Defects in the ORIGINAL PUBLISHED GAME found during encoding - spec #21. Authority ladder (as amended 2026-08-09): official errata > publisher/tournament clarification or the game/module creator's answer > proven outcome-equivalence. 'Declared umpired' is no longer a valid resolution: an unresolvable defect blocks playability until resolved by authority.

list.defect: The printed map gives hex QQ32 blue (Bastion) hexsides; the rulebook's own errata paragraph corrects it: 'The hexsides of QQ32 should be orange (fort); not blue (bastion).'
list.resolution: QQ32 is encoded as a Fort (breach defense 12, Fort missile row). The v3.0.0 module map art already paints QQ32 orange - the module author pre-applied the official errata.
list.authority: Official errata printed in the rulebook [2.15].

list.defect: The two official Q&A documents print the SAME ruling under different rule citations. The General's Question Box (Vol 26 No 4 p.58): '7.311/17.23 Can/must Judaean units leave a ground-level Heavy Infantry ZOC when routing/panicking? A. No.' The 1/6/1992 AH typescript: identical question and answer, cited '7.311/17.3'. The rulings agree; the cross-reference does not.
list.resolution: The ruling is identical in both documents and is enforced: Judaean units in Roman Heavy-Infantry ground-level ZOC do not move when Routed/Panicked (the 7.311 freeze). RETRACTION 2026-08-09: an earlier register entry claimed the two documents answered oppositely; decode-prep 6 re-read both scans (9x off soj_errata1.gif, 300 dpi off The_General_Vol26i4.pdf p.58) and both print 'A. No.' - the contradiction claim was our transcription error. Schachter's design notes (The General 26-4 p.11) confirm the rule as deliberate design.
list.authority: Official Q&A, both documents in agreement; designer's notes corroborate.

list.defect: Both official Q&A documents print a non-responsive answer: '14.2 If as a result of Melee, all units in a fort, testudo or siege engine hex accept a B result, must they all retreat one or two hexes? A. Yes.' - 'Yes' does not choose between one and two.
list.resolution: Read as answering 'must they all retreat (together)?' - yes. The Melee Table's own B text ('Retreat all units one or two hexes') already makes the distance the retreating player's choice; the engine enforces B as: all defending units retreat, each one or two hexes at the owning player's option [14.2].
list.authority: Declared interpretation from the Melee Table's printed text; the Q&A's own wording defect is what this entry registers.

list.defect: The reinforcement rule says the Judaean player 'rolls the dice' (plural) for how many Giora units enter, then 'rolls the die again' (singular) for the entry gate - whether the count roll is one die or two is not defined anywhere in the rules or either official Q&A document.
list.resolution: TWO dice for the count (the game's standard is two d6 [2. COMPONENTS: 'two six-sided dice'; Repair and Elevated Hex Damage rolls are explicitly 'two dice']) and one die for the gate, following the card's own singular/plural distinction. The gate roll's odd/even split is dice-count-invariant, so only the count ever hung on the ambiguity.
list.authority: Declared ruling (2026-08-13), pending module-author/expert review (no official ruling found).

list.defect: The card bars Roman entry of Garrison Areas with examples only: 'Roman entry of Garrison Areas is not allowed (e.g., Romans may never enter P50 or QQ32)' - 'e.g.' leaves the areas' hex extents undefined, and 18.4 names three multi-hex areas (Temple Quarter, Herod's Palace inclusive of the Fortress Triangle and Yafo Gate complex, Antonia Fortress) whose boundaries are drawn nowhere in hex terms.
list.resolution: Prohibited = the nine battlefield-reachable perimeter hexes of the three areas: P50 + Q49 (west, Yafo Gate complex/Fortress Triangle) and MM31, MM32, MM33, NN33, OO33 (Tadi Gate), PP33, QQ32 (east, Antonia Fortress + Temple Quarter north wall). Derivation: 18.3 divides city areas BY walls; 5.6 counts the Temple area's outer walls as Temple-area hexes; the printed map's ANTONIA FORTRESS / TEMPLE QUARTER / TADI GATE / YAFO GATE labels fix which walls bound which area; both card examples are perimeter strongpoints, proving the perimeter reading; every interior hex is off the bounded battlefield. Q49 (Second Wall's southern gate opening into the fortress complex) is the one ambiguous junction, prohibited under the declared ambiguity-goes-prohibited tiebreak. Corollary: both Giora reinforcement entry gates (OO33, Q49) are Roman-prohibited, so the relief-force doors can never be occupied. Consequence carried through the engine: since 11.1 melee eligibility = 'could enter if vacated', Romans can neither enter NOR melee-attack a Garrison hex (missile/rock fire remains legal) - the same reading the two printed example hexes have always had; Judaean entry, deployment and defense there are unrestricted [18.4].
list.authority: Declared ruling (2026-08-12), pending module-author/expert review; the enforced behaviour is strictly a superset of the card's printed examples.

list.defect: Neither the rulebook nor the counter manifest states how many TESTUDO counters the printed mix holds per Legion, and no supply tray or setup places one - so whether 'one testudo formation per Legion at a time' is a physical component limit the gate must enforce is unrecoverable from the printed sources alone (the VASSAL palette is an unlimited supply and proves nothing).
list.resolution: Enforced as ONE INTACT Testudo formation per Legion at a time: rule 2.6's marker figure prints the TESTUDO counter Legion-marked (the sample is the XV counter in XV's colour) and the module supplies exactly one testudo art per Legion (V, X, XII, XV) - consistent with one physical counter each. A BROKEN Testudo does not hold the counter (the Broken Testudo marker is a separate printed counter, 2.6), so a new formation may assemble while a broken one persists. Single-Legion Gallus makes the cross-Legion arm unreachable; the per-Legion (not global) shape is proven by a synthesized second-Legion formation in the validator.
list.authority: Declared ruling (2026-08-12), pending module-author/expert review (ROB_QUESTIONS R2); loosening on Rob's answer never invalidates prior play.

list.defect: The printed game supplies no legend for the staircase symbol (the map's terrain key has 14 entries, none of them Staircase; the TEC likewise), and the module author's own v2.2 changelog concedes 'Stairway location subject to player interpretation'. The designer's notes confirm staircases exist so Romans can seize weakly-held bastions and/or forts, but not WHICH hexsides carry them. Session 1 encoded 20 hexsides by pattern inference whose art measurement finds nothing (10 ABSENT at protrusion 0.0-0.03, 8 AMBIGUOUS at 0.03-0.06 vs the far-higher CONFIRMED band, 2 CONTAMINATED by adjacent structure art).
list.resolution: All 20 doubtful hexsides EXCLUDED; the 27 art-CONFIRMED staircases (plus the art-confirmed Z33-Z34 addition) stand. Full per-hexside list with verdicts and scores: ingest/staircases_evidence.json + ROB_QUESTIONS R4. Consequence: each affected strongpoint (G40, G43, M50, MM31, O50, PP17, PP33, V42, DD19, II27, JJ17, L50, LL30, MM32, MM33, QQ25) carries no staircase, so it cannot be entered from ground level [8.93] or ground-meleed [11.11] - Romans must breach or escalade it. The error mode is deliberately LOUD (a wrongly-excluded real staircase surfaces as a refused legal attack citing this entry), never silent; any hexside the module author confirms is re-added, invalidating no prior play.
list.authority: Declared ruling (2026-08-12), ambiguity-goes-loud tiebreak; pending module-author adjudication (ROB_QUESTIONS R4, full table prepared).

list.defect: The Assault Period Interphase sequence printed in The General Vol 26 No 4 is wrong per the corrected sequence-of-play aid reviewed by developer Don Greenwood (Sinigaglio prep+interphase aid).
list.resolution: Campaign-game scope - not reachable from the Gallus scenario. To be registered in full when the campaign game is encoded; the corrected Greenwood-reviewed sequence is preserved in the validation library (atf_interphase.htm).
list.authority: Developer-reviewed correction (semi-official), pending full campaign encoding.

list.defect: The rulebook names two different markers for the same event. 13.21: an Artillery unit eliminated when Disrupted while already Panicked leaves 'an "Elim" Artillery marker ... on the map to affect stacking until the end of the Assault Period'. 14.5: 'Eliminated Artillery (other than Cauldrons) and Siege Engines are replaced with an appropriate Wreck marker on the map.' The printed counter mix contains BOTH faces (2.6: 'Elim.' is the back of Broken Testudo, row 8; Wreck is the back of Ramp, row 4), so it is cleanly a rules question, not a components shortcut.
list.resolution: The engine drops a single 'elim' marker through its one elimination door on every non-Cauldron Artillery elimination path. Its enforced effects are the two texts' common - and provably entire - Gallus-visible behavior: the marker holds the Artillery stacking slot for the rest of the scenario. Enumeration of every candidate divergence: (1) LOF - Artillery never affects LOF as a unit, and 11.4's 'affect LOF as if the Siege Engine were still there' clause is written for Siege Engine wrecks only; (2) 14.5's 'thereby block the movement of similar units into/through' derives from the stacking effect both texts share; (3) removal timing ('Assault Period' vs the dangling 'Assault Phase', see wreck-removal-assault-phase-reference) is unreachable in a one-Assault-Period scenario. The marker face a physical player sets out is cosmetic to the gate.
list.authority: Proven outcome-equivalence within the Gallus scenario. Marker identity and removal timing escalated to the module author (ROB_QUESTIONS R7) for campaign scope.

list.defect: 14.5 closes: 'Remove the "Wreck" markers at the end of the Assault Phase.' No phase named 'Assault Phase' exists anywhere in the 4.x sequence of play (Rally/Fire/Movement/Melee per side); every other duration in the marker rules (13.21) runs 'until the end of the Assault Period'.
list.resolution: Wrecks persist to the end of the Assault Period, the only defined referent, corroborated by 13.21's parallel wording. In Gallus - a single Assault Period - markers are therefore never removed during play.
list.authority: Dangling reference resolved to the only defined term; 13.21 corroborates. Escalated with R7 for campaign scope.

list.defect: 6.61's exception list omits the Velitae that 16.4 explicitly admits. 6.61: 'Disrupted units may not enter a Testudo hex [Exception: Disrupted HQ may join a Testudo provided the HQ is not Panicked].' 16.4: 'The only Disrupted units with the ability and sufficient MF to form or join Testudo are HQ and Velitae. ... A Disrupted HQ and/or Velitae may join a Testudo if not already fully-occupied.' (Both verified off the page scans, pp.6/12.)
list.resolution: 16.4 governs: it is the dedicated Disruption-Effects clause, names Velitae twice, and its MF observation is exact (Disrupted Velitae MA 6 = the printed 6 MF join cost; Disrupted Heavy Infantry MA 5 cannot pay it). The gate admits Disrupted (not Routed/Panicked) Velitae and non-Panicked HQ joins; 6.61's exception list is read as incomplete.
list.authority: The rulebook's own specific clause over the incomplete general list; the MF arithmetic corroborates. No Q&A entry touches it.

list.defect: 8.8: two Fresh Heavy Infantry declare Testudo at a cost of six MF, '(leaving the Testudo with one MF remaining during that MPh - unless the component units had already used one or two MF before forming Testudo)'. Every printed Heavy Infantry counter and the 2.41 unit diagrams carry Fresh MA 8 (byte-verified against the module counters), so unmoved formers retain 8 - 6 = TWO MF, not one; 'one MF remaining' is consistent only with an MA of 7 that no Heavy Infantry counter has.
list.resolution: The MF arithmetic governs: forming charges 6 MF to each forming unit and the new formation may spend min(Testudo MA 4, lowest Fresh member remainder) that MPh - 2 MF for unmoved formers. The parenthetical's 'one' is an arithmetic slip (its own 'one or two MF already used' range matches MA 8: remainders 1 and 0).
list.authority: Printed counter values (2.41/2.54, module counters byte-verified); validator pins the remainder at exactly 2 MF.
